terms.meaning: a pattern written in symbols that describes a piece of text to search for
a stand-in value that should be replaced before release
a report that flags something harmless

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for files and paths
sections.what: Brings in the Node tools for reading folders and building file paths.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the script must walk folders and read files.

sections.name: findInDir
sections.title: Finds source files recursively
sections.what: Walks through the source folder and every subfolder, collecting TypeScript files.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: the scan must cover the whole app, not one folder.
sections.watch_out: Only files ending in the two TypeScript extensions are included, so other file types are never scanned.

sections.name: suspiciousPatterns
sections.title: Lists the suspicious patterns
sections.what: Defines the search patterns for leftover fake values, including a grade, a coin count, some progress numbers and sample names of people and events.
sections.why: Each pattern targets a value that was likely typed in as demo data.
sections.watch_out: Global flag regular expressions used with a test call can skip matches, so the search result may be incomplete.

sections.name: matches
sections.title: Matches lines and reports them
sections.what: Reads each file line by line and tests every pattern. It skips known harmless cases such as breakpoints, colors and drawing code. It records each remaining match and prints the full list.
sections.why: The skip rules keep the report focused on real placeholder values.
sections.watch_out: A real placeholder that happens to share a line with a skipped word, such as a border class, will be silently hidden.

summary: Scans the source folder for leftover fake data, such as sample names and numbers, and prints each line that looks suspicious.
purpose: Helps find demo or placeholder values before the app is released.
why: Reason not stated in the code. Likely reason: fake values often slip into a release by accident.
how: List every TypeScript file under the source folder. Read each line of each file. Test the line against each suspicious pattern. Skip lines that match known safe cases. Record every remaining match. Print the total and each match.
inputs: All .ts and .tsx files under the source folder of the current project.
outputs: A count and a list of matching lines with file name, line number, pattern name and the line text.
risks: Broad patterns report many lines that are not real problems. Some safe-case filters are long and could hide a real match on the same line.
debug: Run the script from the project root so the source folder is found. If a known fake value is missed, check the pattern and the safe-case filters. If there are too many matches, the filters need tightening.
